manifest.name: POS - HR
manifest.summary: Link module between Point of Sale and HR
manifest.author: Odoo S.A.

models._description: Point of Sale Configuration (+ tiered allowed-employee lists)
Session sales details for a single employee
Point of Sale Orders (+ owning cashier employee)
Point of Sale Payments (+ cashier employee, related from order)
Point of Sale Session (+ currently logged-in cashier)
Bank Statement Line (+ employee who did the cash move)
Point of Sale Orders Report (+ employee dimension)
Daily Sales Report wizard (+ per-employee report option)

behavioral_notes.observation: Which employees may log in to a till is governed by three Many2many lists on pos.config (minimal/basic/advanced access). If all three are empty, every employee can log in (the manifest's 'unlimited number of employees can log on to that till'); if basic_employee_ids is set, pos.config._employee_domain restricts the loaded set to the union of the three lists (plus the till's own user). hr.employee carries the pos.load.mixin contract: _load_pos_data_domain pushes only those allowed employees into the offline client, and _load_pos_data_read derives a per-employee `_role` (admin/manager/minimal/cashier) and ships a SHA1-hashed `_barcode`/`_pin` rather than plaintext. pos.config.write force-adds every group_pos_manager user's employee into advanced_employee_ids (creating an employee record via action_create_employee if the manager has none), so managers always retain till access. None of this list-merge / role-derivation / hashing logic is visible in metadata.

Identity is stamped at three levels. pos.session.employee_id (tracking=True) records the cashier 'who currently uses the cash register' and is written by the OWL app on every cashier switch (PosStore.setCashierUpdateSession). pos.order.employee_id is the owning cashier and feeds a stored `cashier` Char (compute _compute_cashier: employee name, else user name) used as the human label on receipts/reports; pos.payment.employee_id is related=pos_order_id.employee_id (stored, indexed) so payments inherit the order's cashier. pos.session._load_pos_data_models only appends 'hr.employee' to the client payload when config.module_pos_hr is on. At close, get_closing_control_data breaks cash and each non-cash payment method down per employee (_aggregate_payments_amounts_by_employee, with an 'Others' bucket) and aggregates cash in/out moves per employee, enabling a single-employee Z-report (report.pos_hr.single_employee_sales_report). pos.order._prepare_pos_log appends 'Cashier <name>' (from context current_cashier_id) to the chatter audit line. These cross-model attributions are pure Python.

Badge/PIN login is enforced server-side without exposing secrets: get_barcodes_and_pin_hashed gates on group_pos_user, applies record-rule visibility, then returns SHA1 hashes of each employee's barcode and pin (never plaintext) so the browser can match a scanned badge / typed PIN locally. An @api.ondelete guard (_unlink_except_active_pos_session) blocks deleting any employee who could be used by a till with an open session (either an all-employees till or one whose allowed lists contain the employee), raising a UserError listing the offending pos.config(s). This referential-integrity rule and the hash-only credential exposure are invisible to metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: frontend (cashier-switch + login gating OWL layer) -- gap #3 exemplar
behavioral_notes.observation: pos_hr ships almost no UI of its own (1 new component, CashierSelectionPopup) and instead patches ~12 existing POS OWL classes to graft an employee-identity layer onto the standalone offline terminal. The reusable hook useCashierSelector (utils/select_cashier_mixin.js) drives both badge login (useBarcodeReader 'cashier' handler: find employee by SHA1(barcode), prompt for PIN via NumberPopup if `_pin` set) and manual selection (CashierSelectionPopup listing allowed employees, with PIN re-check). LoginScreen is patched so opening the register sets pos.login and Enter submits the PIN; PosStore.setup forces navigation to LoginScreen until hasLoggedIn, persists the connected cashier in sessionStorage (`connected_cashier_<config.id>`), and buffers cashier->session writes while offline, replaying them on the browser 'online' event. setCashier stamps order.employee_id on empty orders and downgrades the numpad out of 'price' mode if the cashier lacks price-control rights; createNewOrder / addLineToCurrentOrder / OrderPaymentValidation.validateOrder all re-assert order.employee_id = current cashier. Per-employee gating is everywhere: Navbar.showBackend and LoginScreen.clickBack only let the cashier whose user_id == the logged-in user reach the backend; employeeIsAdmin (`_role === 'manager'`) gates product creation, payment editing and price control. None of this client-side login/switch/gating flow is reverse-engineerable from Python metadata -- it lives entirely in static/src.

it_architecture.application: pos_hr (auto-install bridge: stamps HR-employee identity onto the Point of Sale terminal -- backend fields + an OWL cashier login/switch + gating layer over the offline POS SPA)
software_services: (no own HTTP/RPC routes; extends point_of_sale via the pos.load.mixin data-load contract and patches the OWL terminal served at /pos/ui)
hr.employee._load_pos_data_domain/_fields/_read (push allowed cashiers + hashed badge/PIN + role into the client)
pos.session.log_partner_message (chatter log keyed to the cashier's contact, called from the client)
logical_data_erm: pos.config -> hr.employee (minimal_employee_ids / basic_employee_ids / advanced_employee_ids: who may log in)
pos.order -> hr.employee (employee_id: owning cashier) -> cashier (stored name)
account.bank.statement.line -> hr.employee (employee_id: who did the cash in/out)
hr.employee -> res.users (user_id, links badge identity to the till's backend user)
hr.employee -> res.partner (work_contact_id, used as chatter message author)
information_flows: depends: point_of_sale (the terminal/session/order it augments), hr (the employee identity it borrows)

load: pos.session._load_pos_data_models adds 'hr.employee' to the client payload only when module_pos_hr is on; _load_pos_data_domain restricts it to the allowed lists; _read ships SHA1(barcode)/SHA1(pin) + derived role
side-effect: OWL cashier switch (PosStore.setCashierUpdateSession) -> write pos.session.employee_id (buffered + replayed when offline)
side-effect: createNewOrder / addLineToCurrentOrder / validateOrder -> stamp pos.order.employee_id = current cashier -> pos.payment.employee_id (related) -> cashier Char on receipts
side-effect: close -> get_closing_control_data aggregates payments + cash moves per employee for a per-cashier Z-report
guard: hr.employee unlink blocked while an employee may be used by a till with an open session
frontend_components: LoginScreen.prototype (PIN entry / openRegister / clickBack -> backend gate)
PosStore.prototype (force LoginScreen until logged in, sessionStorage cashier, offline employee buffer, per-cashier gating)
Navbar.prototype (showBackend / showCreateProductButton gated by cashier user_id + admin role)
ClosePosPopup.prototype / CashMovePopup.prototype / OrderSummary.prototype / ProductInfoPopup.prototype (per-employee data + gating)

capabilities: Authenticate Cashier at the Till (badge / PIN login of an HR employee, no Odoo user per cashier)
Switch Active Cashier mid-session without re-login
Authorize Till Access by Employee (tiered minimal / basic / advanced allow-lists per pos.config)
Attribute Sales, Payments & Cash Moves to the Employee who made them
Gate POS Actions by Employee Role (price control, payment edit, product creation, backend access)
Per-Cashier Sales Reporting (single-employee Z-report / employee dimension on POS analysis)
value_streams: Cashier identity overlay on Sell-at-Counter: employee logs in (badge/PIN) -> rings sales stamped with employee_id -> switches cashier as shifts change -> close yields per-employee cash/payment breakdown
organization: point_of_sale.group_pos_manager (reused; managers auto-added to advanced_employee_ids and mapped to the 'manager'/'admin' client role)
policies: If all employee lists are empty, every employee may log in; otherwise only the union of minimal/basic/advanced (plus the till's user) -- pos.config._employee_domain
Managers (group_pos_manager) are force-added to advanced_employee_ids on write and cannot be demoted to minimal/basic (onchange rules)
Badge/PIN are exposed to the client only as SHA1 hashes and only to group_pos_user
An employee usable by a till with an open session cannot be deleted (ondelete guard)
Only the cashier whose user_id == the logged-in backend user may exit the POS to the backend
stakeholders: Cashier / Sales Clerk (hr.employee, may have no Odoo user)
Payroll / HR (employee mapping; not a runtime dependency here)
metrics: report.pos.order.employee_id (employee dimension on the POS Orders analysis pivot/graph)
get_closing_control_data: cash + per-payment-method amount_per_employee and moves_per_employee at session close

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: pos_hr is the staffing/identity layer of the retail Sell operation in the Point of Sale value chain: it does not itself sell, deliver or post accounting -- it overlays an HR-employee identity onto the existing pos.order/pos.session/pos.config so that the chain's primary checkout act (point_of_sale, APQC 3.0) is performed and attributed by a named cashier who logs in by badge/PIN rather than by holding an Odoo user account. Its value_model is therefore 'chain' (it augments a value-chain primary activity) but its activity_class is 'support': it is a thin (auto-install, route-less, 3-real-model) bridge whose entire contribution is cashier authentication, mid-shift cashier switching, tiered till-access authorization, per-employee sales/cash attribution and role-based action gating -- a workforce/identity enabler around the sale, not the sale or its delivery/AR side-effects. APQC 3.0 (retail operations -- cashier management) is the right home because the capability it adds (manage who staffs and operates the counter) sits squarely on the in-store sell process realized by point_of_sale; it has no inventory (4.0) or finance (9.0) logic of its own beyond stamping employee_id on the cash-move and report rows. The bulk of the module is OWL/JS in static/src patching the offline terminal (gap #3): the login screen, the cashier-selection popup and the per-employee gating live entirely in the browser and are not reverse-engineerable from Python metadata.

standard_capabilities: Log employees into a single shared till by barcode badge and/or PIN, with no per-cashier Odoo user required
Switch the active cashier mid-session from the navbar (CashierSelectionPopup) without closing the register
Restrict till login per pos.config via tiered minimal/basic/advanced employee allow-lists (empty = all employees)
Stamp the owning employee on every pos.order, pos.payment and cash-move statement line; show the cashier name on receipts
Role-based gating in the POS: managers can create products, edit payments and control price; cashiers cannot; only the user-linked cashier reaches the backend
Per-employee closing breakdown and a single-employee daily Z-report; employee dimension on the POS Orders analysis report
Offline-safe identity: hashed badge/PIN shipped to the client, cashier-to-session writes buffered and replayed on reconnect
typical_fits: Retail/restaurant with several clerks sharing one register per shift and accountability per cashier
Sites that want POS staff to authenticate without provisioning an Odoo user/login for each employee
Stores needing manager-only actions (price override, payment edit, product creation) behind a PIN/role
Daily cash reconciliation that must attribute takings to the cashier who collected them
common_gaps: Time & attendance / clock-in tied to POS login (handled by separate hr_attendance / restaurant integrations, not core pos_hr)
Commission or incentive calculation from per-employee POS sales (needs custom or sales-commission dev)
Granular per-action permissions beyond the built-in cashier/manager (admin) split (custom OWL gating)
Strong-auth cashier identification (biometric / external SSO) instead of barcode+PIN
Enforcing the allowed-employee lists server-side for non-UI order creation (the gating is primarily client-side)
drive_hints: odoo shell: cfg = env['pos.config'].search([],limit=1); env['hr.employee'].search(cfg._employee_domain(env.uid))  # who could log into the first till
odoo shell: env['hr.employee'].search([],limit=3).get_barcodes_and_pin_hashed()  # confirm only SHA1 hashes leave the server
launch /pos/ui/<config_id> with pos_hr active -> the terminal opens on LoginScreen demanding a badge scan or PIN before any sale

open_questions: Exact precedence when an employee is added to / removed from the allowed lists while a session is open, and how the client refreshes its loaded employee set.
Whether the allowed-employee restriction and role gating are re-enforced server-side on sync_from_ui, or only in the OWL client (potential bypass for crafted RPC).
Full interaction with pos_restaurant (cashier per floor/table) and hr_attendance (clock-in on POS login) when those bridges are also installed.
Collision/handover behaviour of the sessionStorage `connected_cashier_<config.id>` token across browser tabs and devices on the same till.
Side-effects of auto-provisioning an employee for a manager with none (pos.config.write -> action_create_employee).
